target_customer: Smartphone users wanting free internet voice calls
problem: Calling over mobile data needed a messaging-app-like simplicity; voice calls were costly or hard to set up.
business_model: Free consumer voice-calling app; monetization not found

founders.name: Anuj Jain
previous_startups: Several companies in gaming, messaging and fintech (names and outcomes not given)

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable VoIP over 3G and WiFi with contact detection is hard for one person, though standard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Product had no network scale shown and calls were commodity; Hike bought it for technology to speed its own launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WhatsApp was reported in January 2015 as preparing voice calling; Hike acquired Zip Phone on 2015-01-08, deal terms undisclosed.

market_need_then: Not documented beyond the product premise ('WhatsApp for voice'); no usage figures were found.

brand_strength.rationale: One-person startup with no brand press found; absorbed into Hike.

outcome_analysis: Zip Phone was a one-person YC Summer 2014 voice-calling app acquired by Hike Messenger in January 2015, Hike's first acquisition, to bring free voice calling to market faster. Price and traction were not disclosed. The outcome reads as a technology acquisition rather than a product success, but without terms or usage data that classification is tentative.
notes: Acquisition by Hike announced 2015-01-08 per search results from several outlets (YourStory returned 403 on fetch and was not worked around; digit.in article read). Deal terms undisclosed. The acquihire_soft_landing tag is inferred from reported rationale (technology to speed Hike's launch), not stated outright.
